title: Natural Domain and Graph of the Signum Quotient F(t) = t / |t|
originalTopic: Functions and Graphs: Domain and Graphing
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Find the natural domain and describe the graph of the function F(t) = t / |t|.
finalAnswer: \text{Domain: } (-\infty, 0) \cup (0, \infty); \quad F(t) = 1 \text{ for } t > 0, \; F(t) = -1 \text{ for } t < 0

steps.title: Find the Natural Domain
steps.explanation: The denominator |t| equals zero if and only if t = 0. Thus F(t) is defined for all non-zero real numbers.
steps.why: Division by zero at t = 0 is undefined.

steps.title: Simplify the Formula on Each Branch of the Domain
steps.explanation: For t > 0, |t| = t, so F(t) = t/t = 1. For t < 0, |t| = -t, so F(t) = t/(-t) = -1.
steps.why: Expanding the piecewise definition of |t| reduces the ratio to a constant on each open half-line.

steps.title: Describe the Step Graph
steps.explanation: The graph consists of two horizontal open rays: the horizontal line y = 1 for t > 0 with an open circle at (0, 1), and the horizontal line y = -1 for t < 0 with an open circle at (0, -1).
steps.why: The function is constant on (-inf, 0) and on (0, inf) with a jump discontinuity at t = 0.
